## When to apply
When a sequence of edits has led to build failures, test failures, or a fundamentally wrong approach.

## Steps
1. Recognize when you're in a bad state: multiple failed fix attempts, cascading errors, or wrong architectural approach
2. Use rollback to restore all files to their pre-edit state rather than manually undoing changes
3. After rollback, re-read the relevant code to understand the clean starting state
4. Plan the corrected approach before making any new edits

## Why this matters
Manually undoing a chain of edits is error-prone - you may miss a change or introduce new errors. Rollback atomically restores the known-good state. Starting fresh with a better plan is faster than debugging a broken chain of patches.

## Pitfalls
- Spending 10+ minutes trying to manually fix cascading errors instead of rolling back
- Rolling back without understanding WHY the approach failed, leading to the same mistake
- Not saving your findings/plan to scratchpad before rollback (rollback only affects files, not notes)
description: When edits lead to failures, use rollback to restore files rather than manually undoing each change.
